title: Most Struggling Students Get Incoherent Instruction
author: Natalie Wexler
summary: Struggling students often receive instruction characterized by fragmented, disconnected lessons that prioritize behavior compliance and activity completion over coherent knowledge building. While higher-achieving students get systematic, sequenced instruction built on clear curriculum structures, students with learning difficulties are often shuffled through remedial programs emphasizing isolated skills rather than connected knowledge. This incoherence exacerbates learning difficulties rather than addressing them. Struggling students actually need more coherent, more systematic instruction, not less. Yet current systems often provide the opposite: disconnected activities justified by the belief that struggling students can't handle complexity. This approach guarantees continued struggle because learning requires coherence and connection.
